audit.why: 55.08% over 118 games with TRICKY 7.5/10. Quinn takes level 1 and the level-6 roam window; the turret triangle owns everything between.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows were the exact inverse of both the packet chart and the stored whys — the page gave Heimerdinger level 1 while its own why said Quinn owns it outright.
audit.why: Level 1 he has one turret and nothing else; levels 3-5 are his peak with the triangle plus grenade; 6 is Quinn's roam window; the item stages are genuinely even.
audit.corrected: Six rows flipped as one atomic group in both layers to Quinn / Skill / Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger / Quinn / Skill / Skill, ratings moved to match, and every phases[N].why rewritten to its new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Q-blind' / 'Vault-blind' framing; 'blind a turret with Q'; 'leap over the turret line'; nothing about the grenade cancelling Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Blinding Assault marks an enemy and hinders its vision by Riot's text — nothing in the kits says it affects a turret at all, so that advice is unsupported. Vault is a targeted dash onto an enemy that lands Quinn at her own attack range; it does not vault a wall of turrets. CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stuns on a direct hit and Behind Enemy Lines is a flagged channel, so his 11s grenade or an UPGRADE!!! cast ends her ultimate.
audit.corrected: Removed the turret blind, restated Vault, and put the channel cancel with its 11s number on the interactions line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues — nothing told you what to wait for.
audit.why: The grenade is a flat 11s at every rank and the rockets are 11s at rank 1; those two numbers are the whole timing game.
audit.corrected: Both written into the rewritten why and interaction lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven whys and all three prose stages are written in the first person.
audit.why: The site's voice is second person; this entry reads as a different author.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are mine — my range and Harrier auto-resets shove him off the first creeps before his turrets matter, so trade hard and deny him an early plant. Once he gets a turret or two down and E-grenade online by level 3, the lane flips: the turrets chunk me if I walk up to last-hit and he walls me off the wave. Bait his E stun — if I can blind a turret with Q during a step-up I survive, but never facetank the triangle.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours — your range and Harrier auto-resets shove him off the first creeps before his turrets matter, so trade hard and deny him an early plant. Once he has two turrets down and the grenade online at 3, the lane flips: the turrets chunk you on every last-hit and he walls you off the wave. Bait the 11s grenade out before you step up to trade, and never facetank the triangle.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his peak zone — three turrets plus rocket poke mean I can't freely walk up, and his E grenade into a turret focus can delete me if I overstep. I stop trying to win the standoff and just farm what I can with Q tip. At 6 everything changes: R lets me scout-form past his wall and roam mid or bot, so I take my tempo to the map instead of feeding his turrets free poke.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his peak zone — three turrets plus rocket poke mean you cannot freely walk up, and a grenade stun into turret focus deletes you if you overstep. Stop trying to win the standoff and farm what you can from Blinding Assault's 1025 range. At 6 it changes: Behind Enemy Lines takes you past his wall to mid or bot, so spend tempo on the map, not on his turrets.

edits.before: Late, this is a coinflip that hinges on tempo. Heimer's turret zone and rocket poke are brutal in a static teamfight, and I fall off as a squishy with no front-to-back threat — if the game goes long behind his zone, he wins. My out is the map: I should have used R roams to snowball side lanes and end before his turret walls own every chokepoint. Pick him in the open with E-Vault and Harrier where he has no turrets, never into his triangle.

notes: The stored whys already described the packet's chart correctly while the win/side tokens said the opposite — this entry was the clearest case in the slice of the two layers being written by different passes. Nothing in the kits states whether Blinding Assault's vision hinder affects turrets, so the old 'blind a turret' advice was removed rather than restated. UPGRADE!!! shows range 1 in the kit file, which is a data artefact of a self-cast, so no range was printed for it.
